Note: Genome sizes range from 2 Mb to 4.0 Mb. Plasmids of varying size and copy numbers are expected. The samples could be sent in 2 to 3 batches. Mandatory Requirements & Vendor Compliance Matrix # Parameter Mandatory Specification 1 Technology Long-Read ONLY (ONT R10.4.1 / PacBio HiFi). (Short-read approac h strictly excluded) 2 DNA Extraction (Vendor Vendor must extract Total Genomic DNA (gDNA). Scope) Extraction must retain both high molecular weight chromosomal D NA and all small/large native plasmids (3-4 kb or higher). 3 Prohibition on Size Selec Aggressive size selection techniques (e.g., BluePippin, selective b tion ead-binding) that eliminate DNA fragments less than 8 kb are stric tly prohibited to prevent the loss of plasmids. 4 Coverage Depth Require ≥ 100X average depth across the assembled Main Chromosome, ment calculated after bioinformatics assembly. (Vendor must target sufficient raw data per barcode to ensure the largest possible genome in the batch (4.0 Mb) achieves this 100X threshold).

5 Read Length Metrics N50 ≥ 8 kb representing the native DNA population, achieved via gentle extraction, not by artificially washing away smaller plasmid DNA. 6 Assembly Target 1. Complete, closed, circular main chromosome. 2. Explicit assembly and circularization of all native plasmids. (High-copy plasmid reads must not be used to mathematically infl ate the main chromosome's average coverage). 7 Consensus Accuracy Q30 or higher polished consensus accuracy across the final assem blies. 1. Demultiplexed FASTQ raw data. 8 Key Deliverables 2. Assembled FASTA genomes (Chromosome and Plasmid cont igs explicitly identified). 3. GFF3 / GBK annotation files. 4. Mapped depth statistics (QC report) proving ≥100X for the c hromosome. 5. Primary Statistics report - QA/QC Results. 6. Alignment statistics 7. Coverage analysis 8. Variant analysis 9. Variant annotation 9 Quality Guarantee / Re-r Free re-sequencing (including fresh DNA extraction if necessary) f un or any sample failing the >= 100X chromosomal depth or genome closure requirements. .
